meta.title: LLM Price-Performance Calculator 2026 — Cheapest AI by Arena Score
meta.desc: Find the cheapest LLM that clears your quality bar. Interactive calculator: LMArena Arena scores × real API cost per task, with peak/off-peak pricing, cache-hit discounts and strict CI merging. Free, no signup.
meta.ogTitle: Cheapest LLM at every quality level — Arena Score × real cost
meta.ogDesc: Set your minimum acceptable Arena Score and see the cheapest model that clears it, how much the next tier costs per point, and how peak/off-peak and cache pricing change the answer.

header.sub: cheapest AI model by Arena Score
header.tagline: Drag the capability threshold from highest to lowest and watch each tier's winner update live. This is the lower envelope / Pareto frontier — Your intuition "every capability tier has a best-value model" is mathematically sound, but it needs the right definition (see below). Data: arena.ai/leaderboard, scraped %SCRAPED% (leaderboard dated %CAPTURED%).

intro.h2: Cheapest AI models at every quality level — Arena Score vs. real cost per task
intro.p1: Set the minimum Arena Score you can accept, and it names the cheapest model that clears the bar — plus the marginal $/point to the next tier, corrected for DeepSeek peak/off-peak pricing, expired promos and cache-miss bias. Drag the gold threshold line (or hit ▶ Play) and watch every tier's winner update live.
intro.lnk: Three definitions of "best value" · strict 95% CI mode · prices modeled over a 168-hour week · Method & data sources · JSON (AI-readable) · llms.txt
intro.seoLinks: Static rankings: cheapest for coding · heavy agent workloads · off-peak half-price guide; cheaper alternatives: Kimi K3.1 Pro · DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash · MiniMax-M2.5

ds.licHint:
Open-source-only and all-license are two different boards; their scores are not comparable. Open-source board (?license=open-source) maxes out at 1687 (Kimi K3.1 Pro); the all-license board tops out at 1838 (Claude Fable 5.2 xHigh, $11.04/task) — Claude Opus 5.5 1815, Sonnet 5.5 1772, Gemini 4 Carbon 1768, GPT-6 Astra 1764 are all there. Switch the dataset to the All-license entry.
Note: the all-license board only has the top 41 scraped (Score 1590–1838); the long tail beyond rank 41 is missing. The high-score frontier is unaffected, but "cheapest overall" and "excess score/$" baselines will skew.

modeName.pareto: Threshold: cheapest model with score ≥ T

winner.verdict:
Verdict: below the threshold T = {hi} (range [{lo}, {hi}]),{name} is the cheapest model that clears the capability bar.
It rules the score range [{cov0}, {cov1}] — within it, every higher-scoring model costs more and every cheaper model scores lower (mutually undominated).
winner.degraded: ⚠ Your threshold {hi} exceeds this dataset's top score {smax}; no model qualifies — what follows is the strongest, relatively cheapest one.
winner.bandNotOk: ⚠ Its score {s} is below your lower bound {lo}: no Pareto-optimal model exists in [{lo}, {hi}] because the stronger tier costs more and the cheaper tier scores lower. This is a blind spot of range-style questions — threshold mode only needs one T.
winner.swing: Weekly price swing: this champion's own cost bottoms at {lo} on {loDow} {loHr}:00 UTC and peaks at {hi} on {hiDow} {hiHr}:00 UTC ({spread}× apart). Scheduling tasks into off-peak windows is a free {pct}% discount at this threshold.
winner.nextUp: ↑ Next tier up: {name} ({pts} pts, {cost}) → pay {dc} more for +{ds} pts; marginal price {per}/pt.
winner.nextUpExpensive: This tier is expensive — only worth it if you truly need the capability.
winner.nextUpNone: ↑ Next tier up: none — it's already this dataset's capability ceiling.
winner.downOne: ↓ One tier down: {name} ({pts} pts, {cost}) → save {dc} but lose {ds} pts; i.e. giving up {per} pts per dollar saved.
winner.downTooMuch: Too much capability given up — the saving isn't worth it.
winner.downAcceptable: If budget is tight, this tier is acceptable.
winner.verdictRatio: Verdict: within the score range [{lo}, {hi}] ({n} models in range), ranked by {basis}, the top model is {name} = {val}.
winner.noInBand: Note: no qualifying model in range; this result is from the full domain.
winner.butNote: But note: {name} scores higher ({s}) at a marginal price of {per}/pt. The top "score per $" model is often not the one you should use — it's just the cheapest per point, and may lack absolute capability.
winner.biasedWarn: ⚠ Modes ② and ③ are systematically biased: Arena Score is a Bradley-Terry-style rating with a ~1000+ baseline offset, so ② "score per $" almost always picks cheap models; ③ subtracts the practical 1200 floor to cancel the offset, getting closer to true marginal value.
winner.lowSampleWarn: Sample too small — this "value champion" may be pure noise. Don't make purchasing decisions on it.
winner.costMissing: Cost/Task missing — Arena doesn't publish this model's median task cost, so it can't take part in value comparisons.

cache.off: Off → all input tokens bill at cache-miss prices — exactly Arena's leaderboard Cost/Task basis.
cache.hitHead: Hit rate {h}%: {h}% of input tokens bill at cache-read prices, {m}% at (write-multiplier-inclusive) miss prices; output tokens are never discounted, so even a 100% hit rate can't reach zero.
cache.srcCounts: {pub} models in the candidate set use published cache prices, {est} estimated at 10%{na}.
cache.wmNote: Anthropic / OpenAI bill cache writes separately (= 1.25× input price) and the missed share is paid at the write price; other providers charge no write fee.
cache.missBasis: Note: Arena's Cost/Task is computed at cache-miss prices (the Agent board's inferred $4/$20 list prices are the proof), so enabling the cache discount is a hypothetical — "if your workload really hits this often" — not the board's own meaning.
cache.osHintHead: Output share decides how a "unit-price change" converts into a "Cost/Task change". Default 8% = input:output 11:1, from measured inference on 14 Agent-board models (ratios 3.8–17.9×).
cache.osHintOff: With cache discount off, DeepSeek's peak/off-peak moves input and output proportionally and this slider has no effect on it; it only matters for corrections like GLM's input ×3 / output ×2.8.
cache.osHintOn: With cache discount on, this slider becomes critical: cache discounts input only, so the higher the output share, the thinner the discount. At the same 95% hit rate, DeepSeek-20261017 saves 86% at w=2%, 68% at w=8% (default), 55% at w=15%, 40% at w=25%, and only 25% at w=40%.
cache.adjAllOff: All corrections off → the board as listed. Tick any rule above to see time effects.
cache.adjNone: No model in the current candidate set is affected by the enabled corrections ({rules}).
cache.adjHead: {peak} · {dow} {hr}:00 UTC: {n} models in the candidate set get rewritten →
cache.costCellWhy: Cache hit {h}%: read price {pc}/M ({src}), write multiplier {wm}×

glm53flash_nov.name: GLM-5.3-Flash $0.02/$0.07 vs official $0.15/$0.50, no promo notice (uncertain)

No promo announcement or end date anywhere; the launch blog only says (discounted) for $0.045/task. $0.02/$0.07 closely matches the OpenRouter batch tier ($0.023/$0.068), so this may be a mis-scraped tier or a short unannounced promo. interact.play: ▶ Play: sweep the threshold from highest to lowest
interact.modeHintPareto: Your original idea. Fix threshold T, take the cheapest model among those with score ≥ T. Sweep T downward and the winner sequence is the Pareto lower envelope. The only mathematically self-consistent definition (= capability maximization under a cost constraint).
interact.modeHintRatio: Score ÷ Cost. Strongly biased toward cheap models because Arena scores carry a ~1200 baseline offset (the numerator is artificially inflated). For rough comparison only.
interact.modeHintBaseline: (Score − 1200) ÷ Cost. Arena BT scores have a ~1200 practical floor (below it ≈ random); subtracting it yields "how much real capability gain each dollar buys". Still biased toward cheap models — which is exactly why Threshold mode is the decision-grade definition.
interact.alertTiers: Switch to ① Threshold mode first
interact.tooFewRows: Only parsed {n} rows — check this is an arena.ai leaderboard table (needs Score / Cost/Task columns)
interact.customNote: from data you pasted in this session
interact.noCostParsed: ⚠ Parsed {n} models, but the Cost/Task column is entirely empty — without costs there's no value analysis (the WebDev · HTML board on arena.ai is exactly like this). The dataset was added: you can view score rankings, but the frontier will be empty.
interact.addedOk: ✓ Added {n} models ({wc} with cost data). Custom datasets are lost on reload — save them with "Export CSV".

faq.q: Why doesn't the leaderboard price match my real cost?
faq.a: Board prices assume 0% cache hits and mix peak/off-peak conventions in one table. This tool recomputes your real per-task cost at the cache-hit rate you set (95% by default) and the hour you pick, with published read-ratios and write multipliers applied per model.

faq.q: How are DeepSeek-style off-peak half prices handled?
faq.a: Every model's cost is rendered as a 168-hour weekly curve from each vendor's published peak/off-peak schedule (UTC). The best-value ranking can switch between current-hour, peak and off-peak conventions, so a nightly batch job is priced at nightly rates.
Arena scores carry statistical noise: tiers whose 95% confidence intervals overlap are merged in strict mode, so you don't pay a premium for a ranking difference the data can't support.

faq.q: Is my $20/month plan cheaper than paying per token?
faq.a: It depends on your volume. The break-even calculator compares your plan fee with the cheapest API above a quality bar at your daily task count, including peak/off-peak pricing and cache discounts. Break-even = plan fee divided by API per-task cost, expressed in tasks per day.
